title: Parametrized Tests
description: Two tests that run one body across a table of input-output pairs, using @pytest.mark.parametrize instead of copying the same test body for every pair.

steps.description: This file imports `pytest` and `run`. The page says to use `@pytest.mark.parametrize` when you have a table of input-output pairs that all exercise the same code path, instead of copying the same test body.

`@pytest.mark.parametrize("src,expected", [...])` gives the test below a list of pairs. Each pair is a source string and the value it should produce. `test_arithmetic_ops` takes `src` and `expected` and asserts `run(src) == expected`. The table covers the four operators, precedence (`3 + 4 * 2` gives 11), and parentheses (`(3 + 4) * 2` gives 14).
The second decorator does the same for conditionals. The four pairs run the `true` and `false` branches, a comparison that is true, and a comparison that is false.

steps.question: The page says pytest reports each combination as what, so you see exactly which input failed?
